routes.name: Berkeley Fire Trail Loop
routes.summary: Classic UC Berkeley trail run. Dirt fire road climb with city + Bay views from Grizzly Peak.
routes.best_time: Sunset for Bay views; early morning for shade.

routes.name: Lake Merritt Loop
routes.summary: Flat 3.4-mile loop around Lake Merritt. Necklace of lights, paddle boats, locals everywhere.

routes.name: Marina Green to Fort Point
routes.summary: Flat run along the bay from Marina Green past Crissy Field to Fort Point under the Golden Gate.

routes.name: Stanford Dish Loop
routes.summary: Rolling hills past the radio telescope dish. Mostly paved, open grassland. Gates close at sunset.

routes.name: Lands End Trail
routes.summary: Cliffside trail above the Pacific. Mile Rock, Sutro Baths ruins, clear view of the Golden Gate.

routes.name: Sawyer Camp Trail
routes.summary: Crystal Springs reservoir trail. Paved, gentle, lots of shade. Wildlife sightings common.
routes.best_time: Early morning for cool temps and turkey sightings.

routes.name: Lafayette–Moraga Trail
routes.summary: Converted rail trail through suburban hills. Mostly flat, paved end-to-end.

routes.name: Stevens Creek Trail
routes.summary: Paved creekside trail from Bay shoreline through Mountain View. Bikes welcome too.

routes.name: Iron Horse Trail
routes.summary: Massive rail trail running through Concord, Walnut Creek, Danville. Pick any segment.

routes.name: Marin Headlands Loop
routes.summary: Cross the GG Bridge, climb to Hawk Hill, descend to Rodeo Beach, return via Conzelman.

routes.name: Mount Tamalpais Loop
routes.summary: Big day out: up Hwy 1 to Mt Tam summit via Pantoll, down Bolinas-Fairfax.
routes.best_time: Dry months; check fire road status.

routes.name: Three Bears Loop
routes.summary: Local cycling classic — three rolling climbs through ranch country. Group ride staple.

routes.name: Mt Diablo Summit Ride
routes.summary: The Bay Area benchmark climb. Either south or north gate, both deliver.

routes.name: Old La Honda Climb
routes.summary: The legendary OLH climb. ~3.5 miles, narrow, wooded, perfect PR road.
routes.best_time: Dry days; pavement is rough when wet.

routes.name: Nicasio Reservoir Loop
routes.summary: Rolling rural roads through dairy country and reservoirs. Coffee stop in Nicasio square.

routes.name: Calaveras Reservoir Loop
routes.summary: Quiet road past Calaveras Reservoir. Steady climbs, smooth pavement, near-zero mid-week traffic.

routes.name: Skyline Boulevard Ridge Ride
routes.summary: Hwy 35 along the spine of the Peninsula. Redwood tree tunnels, big views.

routes.name: Highway 1: Pacifica → Half Moon Bay
routes.summary: Pacific coast cruise. Tom Lantos tunnels then cliffs all the way to Half Moon Bay.

routes.name: Highway 1: Stinson → Bodega Bay
routes.summary: Stinson Beach to Bodega Bay. Curves, cliffs, oyster shacks. Half a day, easy.

routes.name: Skyline Boulevard Drive
routes.summary: Crest of the Peninsula. Sweeping curves, redwood overhangs, every motorcyclist's Saturday.

routes.name: Mt Tam Summit Drive
routes.summary: Pantoll to East Peak. Hairpins, redwoods, the whole Bay laid out below.

routes.name: Page Mill Road
routes.summary: Steep climb from 280 up to Skyline. Tight, technical, single-lane in places.

routes.name: Niles Canyon Road
routes.summary: Hwy 84 through Niles Canyon. Tight river curves, watch for cyclists.

routes.name: Hwy 9: Felton → Saratoga
routes.summary: Redwoods, hairpins, summit at Skyline. Classic two-lane mountain road.

routes.name: Mount Hamilton Road
routes.summary: 365 turns to the Lick Observatory at the summit. Long, scenic, almost nobody on it.
routes.best_time: Clear nights for stargazing at the summit.

routes.name: Calaveras Road Drive
routes.summary: Reservoir-side cruise from Sunol to Milpitas. Quiet, sweeping.

routes.name: Embarcadero Walk
routes.summary: Ferry Building to Pier 39 along the bay. Sea lions, sourdough, sailboats.

routes.name: Sausalito Waterfront
routes.summary: Bridgeway from downtown to the houseboats. Boutiques, sea lions, ferry views.

routes.name: Palo Alto Baylands
routes.summary: Boardwalk and levee paths through tidal marsh. Egrets, herons, jets overhead.

routes.name: Berkeley Marina · Cesar Chavez
routes.summary: Cesar Chavez Park loop. Open grass, fly your kite, dog-watch, sunset views back to SF.

routes.name: Mt Tam East Peak
routes.summary: Short out-and-back to the East Peak fire lookout. Highest point in Marin with 360° views.

routes.name: Dipsea Trail
routes.summary: Oldest trail race in the country. Stairs, redwoods, ocean view drop to Stinson Beach.

routes.name: Steep Ravine Loop
routes.summary: Pantoll loop via Steep Ravine and Matt Davis. Wooden ladder in the redwoods, ocean views.
routes.best_time: Wet season — waterfall is best after rain.

routes.name: Mission Peak
routes.summary: Steep grind to the summit pole. Selfie line at the top. Earlier = quieter.

routes.name: Mt Diablo Summit Trail
routes.summary: Mitchell Canyon to summit. Long climb, huge views — Sierra on a clear day.

routes.name: Sweeney Ridge
routes.summary: Ridge hike where Portolá first spotted SF Bay in 1769. Open, windy, panoramic.
routes.best_time: Foggy days are atmospheric, clear days are huge views.

routes.name: Russian Ridge Loop
routes.summary: Rolling grassland ridge, wildflowers in spring, views to both bay and ocean.

routes.name: Berry Creek Falls (Big Basin)
routes.summary: Old-growth redwoods to a waterfall. Long day, mostly shaded.

routes.name: China Camp Bay View Trail
routes.summary: Single-track through oak woodland with constant bay glimpses. Hike or trail-run friendly.

routes.name: Redwood Road
routes.summary: Tight, tree-canopied switchbacks climbing out of Oakland into the Redwood Regional Park ridge. Short, fast, addictive — feels like a backyard race stage.
routes.best_time: Early Sunday morning before park traffic and cyclists wake up.

routes.name: Skyline Boulevard (CA‑35)
routes.summary: The Peninsula's classic ridge run. Long, flowing, redwood-shaded sweepers connecting Hwy 92 down to Saratoga Gap. Patrolled but iconic.
routes.best_time: Dawn weekday — fog clears, no enforcement, no cars.

routes.name: Mount Hamilton Road via Quimby
routes.summary: Quimby is the spicy way up Hamilton — short, brutal switchbacks with steep drop-offs, then a ridge run to Lick Observatory. The full San Jose → Livermore traverse is a half-day epic.
routes.best_time: Clear weekday mornings. Sunset at Lick is the bonus.

routes.name: Highway 9 — Los Gatos to Santa Cruz
routes.summary: Wide, fast, redwoods-and-creek alpine-feeling descent through Boulder Creek. More flow than technical, but the scenery does heavy lifting.
routes.best_time: Off-peak weekdays — coastal commuters fill it on weekends.

routes.name: Palomares Road
routes.summary: Hidden one-lane-feeling connector between Castro Valley and Sunol. Tight, low-speed, technical. Great for chassis feel, not for pace.

routes.name: Panoramic Highway
routes.summary: Mt Tam ridge to Stinson Beach. Ocean reveals between every other corner. The best photo road on this list.
routes.best_time: Golden hour. Avoid summer weekends (Stinson traffic).

routes.name: Silverado Trail
routes.summary: The fast alternative to Hwy 29 through Napa. Open vineyards, wide shoulders, long sight lines, third-gear sweepers all the way to Calistoga.

routes.name: Napa–Lake Berryessa Loop
routes.summary: Loops Napa up over the eastern hills, down to Berryessa, back through Pope Valley. Mix of wide ridge and tight technical sections — the most varied road on this list.
routes.best_time: Spring weekdays — green hills, dry pavement, no boats.

routes.name: Mines Road
routes.summary: Livermore down to San Antonio Valley and onward to Mt Hamilton — the long, lonely backbone of East Bay touge. Hours of empty pavement, ranch land, and zero traffic.
routes.best_time: Sunday morning. Stop at The Junction for breakfast.

routes.name: Wildcat Canyon Run
routes.summary: The Berkeley student's home touge. Steep switchbacks up Marin Ave, a ridge cruise along Grizzly Peak Blvd with the entire Bay laid out below, and a drop into Tilden Park. Short, technical, and walking distance from campus.
routes.best_time: Sunday morning before the cyclists, or sunset for the skyline.

routes.name: Grizzly Peak
routes.summary: A genuinely world-class run if you catch it empty. Up from the flats onto the Grizzly Peak ridge, the spine of the Berkeley hills, with the entire Bay laid out below. The corner sequence is up there with anywhere — flowing, rhythmic, scenery on every apex. Honest 5/5 road. The only reason it isn't rated 5: it's almost never empty. Walking distance from north campus is a blessing and a curse.
routes.best_time: Late night only. The road is busy with cyclists, joggers, drivers, and lookouts every other hour of the day. After ~10pm midweek it finally clears out and the road shows what it is.

routes.name: Pinehurst
routes.summary: The legendary East Bay touge. Single-lane redwood tunnel, no centerline, off-camber decreasing-radius corners stacked one after the next. Locals run it hard. There's a meet every Friday night — show up clean, don't be the loud one, and ride along before you set times. Drop bumpers stay on the road.
routes.best_time: Friday night meets if you know the regulars. Sunday mornings if you want it empty. Avoid wet — the moss never dries out under the canopy.

routes.name: Highway 45 — Sacramento River Road
routes.summary: The classic NorCal roll-race road. Long, flat, dead-straight ag highway from Knights Landing through Grimes, Colusa, and Princeton up to Hamilton City. Decent pavement most of the way, almost zero traffic after dark.
routes.best_time: Late night, summer / dry season. AVOID winter — Sacramento Valley fog kills people here annually.

routes.name: Highway 162 — West of Willows
routes.summary: Long flat straight section heading from Willows toward the foothills at Elk Creek. Very empty after dark. Good roll-racing surface with predictable sight lines.

routes.name: CR 99W — Glenn County Grid
routes.summary: County Road 99W runs straight up the valley parallel to I-5 and Hwy 99. Graph-paper ag survey grid — pavement quality varies between rice paddies and orchards. Pick a clean stretch and you've got miles of nothing.
routes.best_time: Late night, dry. Scout in daylight to find the best-paved sections.

routes.name: Highway 139 — Susanville to Tulelake
routes.summary: If you really want to go where people don't, this is it. Long high-desert straights through the far northeastern corner of California. Hours from any city, almost no traffic, big skies. Pavement quality is hit-or-miss.
routes.best_time: Late summer night. Any other time the weather + remoteness is a real risk.

routes.name: Sherman Island Cross Road
routes.summary: Straight east-west shot across Sherman Island. Very little parking and signage discourages stopping — that's exactly why it's empty. Delta levee road. Many islands here sit 10–25 ft below sea level behind the levees, so you're driving on top of an embankment with water on both sides — often no shoulder, no guardrail. Going off the edge is a real consequence. Fog rolls in fast off the water at night.
routes.best_time: Late night, dry. Avoid winter fog.

routes.name: Sherman Island East Levee Road
routes.summary: Connects in a ~10-mile loop. Narrower than the cross road but with very long straight sections along the levee. Delta levee road. Many islands here sit 10–25 ft below sea level behind the levees, so you're driving on top of an embankment with water on both sides — often no shoulder, no guardrail. Going off the edge is a real consequence. Fog rolls in fast off the water at night.

routes.name: Highway 160 — Antioch Bridge to Rio Vista
routes.summary: Runs north along the Sacramento River from the Antioch Bridge up to Rio Vista. Flat, long well-paved straightaways. The Delta backbone road. Delta levee road. Many islands here sit 10–25 ft below sea level behind the levees, so you're driving on top of an embankment with water on both sides — often no shoulder, no guardrail. Going off the edge is a real consequence. Fog rolls in fast off the water at night.

routes.name: Twitchell Island Road
routes.summary: Turn off Hwy 160 onto Twitchell Island. Remote and dead-quiet at night — you'll see basically no one. Delta levee road. Many islands here sit 10–25 ft below sea level behind the levees, so you're driving on top of an embankment with water on both sides — often no shoulder, no guardrail. Going off the edge is a real consequence. Fog rolls in fast off the water at night.

routes.name: Jersey Island Road
routes.summary: Off Bethel Island Road. Dead-ends but the run out is long, flat, and you'll see basically no one after 9pm. Delta levee road. Many islands here sit 10–25 ft below sea level behind the levees, so you're driving on top of an embankment with water on both sides — often no shoulder, no guardrail. Going off the edge is a real consequence. Fog rolls in fast off the water at night.

routes.name: Hollister Hills SVRA
routes.summary: Largest OHV park in the Bay Area. 6,800 acres of trails for 4x4s, dirt bikes, UTVs. Beginner to expert lines.

routes.name: Carnegie SVRA
routes.summary: 1,500 acres of rolling hills for dirt bikes, ATVs, 4x4s. MX track + open-area free riding.
routes.best_time: Weekday for solitude; rains close it fast.

routes.name: Prairie City SVRA
routes.summary: MX tracks, peewee track, 4x4 area, rock crawl. Year-round park near Sacramento.

routes.name: Clear Creek Management Area
routes.summary: 75,000 acres of remote BLM land for OHV. Permit required. Big, lonely, technical.

routes.name: Rubicon Trail
routes.summary: The iconic American off-road trail. 22 miles of granite slabs, boulder gardens, slow rock-crawling.
routes.best_time: Late July through October when snow clears.

routes.name: Fordyce Creek Trail
routes.summary: One of California's toughest 4x4 trails. Winches mandatory. Deep water crossings, vertical climbs.

routes.name: Frank Raines OHV
routes.summary: 1,300 acres of OHV trails in the Diablo Range foothills. Dirt bikes, ATVs, 4x4s, all welcome.
routes.best_time: Spring; summer is hot and dusty.

routes.name: Stonyford OHV
routes.summary: Mendocino National Forest's premier OHV area. 200+ miles of trails for moto and 4x4. Vast and varied.

routes.name: Cow Mountain OHV
routes.summary: BLM-managed OHV area east of Ukiah. South side has tougher technical trails; north side is open recreation.

routes.name: Foresthill Divide Road
routes.summary: Mostly dirt road through the Sierra foothills. Stock 4WDs can do it; gravel and washboards but no boulders.

routes.name: Oceano Dunes SVRA
routes.summary: The only state park where you can drive on the beach. Sand dunes for ATV / dune buggy / 4x4. Aired-down tires required.

routes.name: Saline Valley Road
routes.summary: 92 miles of remote dirt road through Death Valley's most isolated valley. Hot springs at the end. Cell-dead, prepared-driver only.
